assessments.reasoning: The six verified publisher ranges establish which form is being licensed and place both subsections under the same distribution trigger. Section 3.2(b) expressly protects rights in the source, which resolves the proposed restriction independently of source availability.

challenge.method: Compared two hypothetical executable licenses accompanying timely source access. One preserves MPL source rights. The other purports to forbid redistribution of the covered source.
challenge.results: Different executable terms can satisfy section 3.2(b) in the first case. The attempted restriction defeats the condition in the second, even if the recipient has already downloaded the source or the restriction proves unenforceable.

limitations: The permission concerns the executable license. Its application depends on what the terms actually say about source rights and how the distributor provides access.
reasoning: Section 3.2(b) permits MPL distribution or different sublicense terms for the executable. The condition reaches even an attempt by the executable license to alter or limit the recipient’s MPL rights in the covered source. Section 3.2(a) applies alongside that permission.
